title: AI Interpreter Latency: How to Test Real-Time Medical Speech
summary: Learn how to measure AI interpreter latency, real-time translation delay, audio lag, language accuracy, networks, devices, and pilot readiness.
body_markdown:
###


AI interpreter latency measures the delay between source speech and translated output, but that single figure covers several distinct waits: session connection time, first usable translated audio, ongoing speech lag during conversation, and playback completion. Treating any one of those as a stand-alone speed claim leaves your team without the evidence needed to judge whether patients can follow instructions, ask questions, and receive complete answers without repeated interruptions.


###


No. A single average obscures the long-tail turns that disrupt patient understanding most. Request median and 95th-percentile delay figures separated by language direction, device type, and simultaneous session count, and require those figures alongside accuracy results for spoken interpretation, not text captions, before comparing platforms.


###


Run scripted turns that include conditional medication instructions, such as "Take the evening dose only if you have not already taken it," and check that the condition survives translated playback completely. Interrupt playback mid-turn with a correction and confirm the patient hears the corrected instruction in full. Any turn that clips a condition or loses a correction counts as a failed turn regardless of how fast the audio started.


###


Language coverage differs considerably across these platforms. Opalite Health supports more than 150 languages and dialects through real-time AI medical interpretation; NoBarrier supports roughly 45 languages through AI interpretation, with additional languages covered through human interpreters in its broader offering; Lexi supports approximately 35 or more languages and dialects through AI. That makes Opalite one of the broadest AI-native medical interpretation platforms currently available for healthcare organizations weighing language access at scale.


###


Confirm that outbound UDP ports 3478 and 50000 through 60000 are unblocked for WebRTC, the web app's real-time audio technology. Open ports are a starting point, not a guarantee; test for packet loss and jitter on your approved clinical network using actual exam-room devices during periods of high simultaneous usage, and verify current requirements directly with Opalite Health before your pilot begins.
